questions.q: What is the next number in the arithmetic sequence: $4, 11, 18, 25, \dots$?
In an arithmetic sequence where the first term is $3$ and the common difference is $4$, what is the $15^{\text{th}}$ term?
What is the sum of the first $20$ positive even integers ($2 + 4 + 6 + \dots + 40$)?
questions.answer: Formula for the sum of the first $n$ even integers: $S_n = n(n + 1)$. Here $n = 20$, so $S_{20} = 20 \times 21 = 420$.

questions.q: What is the next term in the geometric sequence: $3, 6, 12, 24, \dots$?
A bacterial culture doubles in number every $20$ minutes. If there are initially $100$ bacteria, how many will there be after $2$ hours?
questions.answer: $2$ hours $= 120$ minutes. Number of doubling cycles $= \frac{120}{20} = 6$. Population $= 100 \times 2^6 = 100 \times 64 = 6400$.

questions.q: What is the $6^{\text{th}}$ term of the sequence: $2, -6, 18, -54, \dots$?
Find the missing number in the sequence: $2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, \dots$?
questions.answer: This is a Fibonacci pattern where each term is the sum of the two preceding terms: $13 + 21 = 34$.

questions.q: What is the next number in the pattern: $1, 4, 9, 16, 25, \dots$?
Find the next term in the sequence: $2, 5, 11, 23, 47, \dots$?
questions.answer: Each term is generated by multiplying the preceding term by $2$ and adding $1$: $47 \times 2 + 1 = 94 + 1 = 95$.

questions.q: If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be $100$ days from now?
questions.answer: Days of the week repeat every $7$ days. Divide $100 \div 7 = 14$ with remainder $2$. Two days after Tuesday is Thursday.

questions.q: A light flashes every $12$ seconds, and a second light flashes every $18$ seconds. If they flash together right now, after how many seconds will they flash together again?
questions.answer: The lights flash together at multiples of the least common multiple: $\text{LCM}(12, 18) = 36$ seconds.

questions.q: In a repeating decimal $0.\overline{142857}$, what is the $50^{\text{th}}$ digit after the decimal point?
questions.answer: The repeating block has length $6$ ($1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7$). Dividing $50 \div 6 = 8$ with remainder $2$. The $2^{\text{nd}}$ digit in the cycle is $4$... wait, the $4^{\text{th}}$ is $8$! $50 = 6 \times 8 + 2$. The $2^{\text{nd}}$ digit is $4$.
